label: Toggle crossplay
summary: Switches the multiplayer crossplay setting on or off.
details: Going by its name, it belongs to the multiplayer configuration of the game's interface. It returns nothing; it only does something when called. Vanilla texts and GUI files do not use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Toggle auto-accept hot join
summary: Switches the multiplayer setting that accepts late-joining players without asking the host on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Auto-accept Hot Join" box of the multiplayer setup window, reached as `MultiplayerSetupWindow.AccessMPConfig`. With the setting on, the host is not asked to accept each player who joins after the game has started.

label: Window itself
summary: Gives the Manage Tax Slots window itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf (for example PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf passed as an argument), it returns a reference to the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the Manage Tax Slots window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the tax slots window. It returns nothing.

label: Liege
summary: A character that the Manage Tax Slots window uses as its data, which by its name is the liege (the ruler above).
details: It returns a character. Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the tax slots window, so everything inside refers to that character. That the character is the liege comes from the name; the game does not say whose liege.

label: Tax slot items
summary: The list of tax slots shown in the Manage Tax Slots window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the window, so the list shows one entry per item it returns. That these items are tax slots comes from the name. The return type is not registered in the documentation.

label: Total levy breakdown
summary: The step-by-step breakdown of the total levy shown in the Manage Tax Slots window.
details: It returns a value breakdown (a number together with the parts it is made of). Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the window. That it is about levy (troops raised from vassals) comes from the name.

label: Total tax breakdown
summary: The step-by-step breakdown of the total tax shown in the Manage Tax Slots window.
details: It returns a value breakdown (a number together with the parts it is made of). Vanilla uses it as a data context in the window. That it is about tax comes from the name.

label: Total tax slots breakdown
summary: The step-by-step breakdown of the total number of tax slots shown in the Manage Tax Slots window.
details: It returns a value breakdown (a number together with the parts it is made of). Vanilla uses it as a data context in the window. That it is about the number of tax slots comes from the name.

label: Remove tax collector
summary: Removes the tax collector from the given tax slot item.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click and passes the tax slot item of that entry (TaxSlotItem.AccessSelf). That it removes a collector comes from the name. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tax slot item whose collector is removed.
fields.values: a tax slot item, as vanilla passes TaxSlotItem.AccessSelf

label: Reset tax slots
summary: Resets something in the Manage Tax Slots window; going by its name, the changes made there.
details: Nothing in vanilla calls it on this type. Other types have a Reset function (an amenities and a message settings window), but that is no proof for this one, so the meaning rests on the name.

label: Window itself
summary: Gives the Manage Tax Slots window itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Auto-assign is on
summary: Whether the auto-assign option is switched on in the Manage Tax Slots window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a checkbox that is toggled by ToggleAutoAssign. What auto-assign does exactly (presumably fills tax slots by itself) comes from the name.

label: Toggle auto-assign
summary: Switches the auto-assign option of the Manage Tax Slots window on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it on click of the checkbox whose checked state comes from ShouldAutoAssign. It returns nothing.

label: Mandate itself
summary: Gives the mandate itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns a reference to the object it is called on. Vanilla uses Mandate in the diarchy window. The game documents nothing more.

label: Description
summary: The description text of a mandate.
details: Vanilla shows it under the mandate's name in the tooltip of the diarchy window. It returns text.

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of a mandate.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an icon in the diarchy window. The return type is not registered in the documentation.

label: Name
summary: The display name of a mandate.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading of the mandate tooltip in the diarchy window. It returns text.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the mandate has an icon.
details: Going by its name, it is a yes/no check. Vanilla uses the same name on other types (game concepts, laws, situation phases) to decide whether an icon is shown, but not on mandates.

label: Mandate itself
summary: Gives the mandate itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument in the diarchy window, for example to IsMandateActive and SetMandate, so those functions know which mandate a row stands for.

label: Editor mode itself
summary: Gives the map content editor mode itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. It belongs to the game's internal map content editor tooling. The game documents nothing more.

label: Map content editor active
summary: Whether the map content editor is the tool chosen in the map editor.
details: The map editor is the game's built-in tool for editing the map. Vanilla uses this as the pressed state of its toolbox button with the tooltip "Map Content Editor".

label: Editor mode itself
summary: Gives the map content editor mode itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Editor options itself
summary: Gives the map content editor options itself, so they can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Apply changes
summary: Applies the changes made in the map content editor.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Apply Changes" button of the map content editor (a tool of the game's built-in map editor). The button works only when the current layer has changes and they can be applied; its tooltip comes from GetApplyButtonDescription.

label: Can apply changes
summary: Whether the changes in the map content editor can be applied right now.
details: Vanilla enables the "Apply Changes" button only when this and CurrentLayerHasChanges are both true. What can block applying is not stated.

label: Can erase
summary: Whether the eraser of the map content editor can be used right now.
details: Vanilla enables the eraser button only when this and IsEraserModeAllowed are both true. The eraser appears only on pixel-based layers. What makes erasing impossible is not stated.

label: Can group
summary: Whether a grouping operation (adding to or removing from a group) is possible right now.
details: Going by its name and the neighbouring add-to-group and remove-from-group modes of the same type. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Layer has changes
summary: Whether the layer open in the map content editor has changes not yet applied.
details: Vanilla enables both the "Apply Changes" and the "Discard Changes" buttons only while this is true.

label: Discard changes
summary: Throws away the changes made in the map content editor that were not applied.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Discard Changes" button, which works only while the current layer has changes.

label: Add-to-group help text
summary: The tooltip text of the map content editor's add-to-group button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the add-to-group button (brush-plus icon), which is shown on layers that are not pixel-based.

label: Apply button help text
summary: The tooltip text of the map content editor's "Apply Changes" button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the "Apply Changes" button, which is enabled only while the current layer has changes and they can be applied.

label: Eraser help text
summary: The tooltip text of the map content editor's eraser button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the eraser button, which is shown on pixel-based layers.

label: Selection mode help text
summary: The tooltip text of the map content editor's selection mode button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the button that turns on the selection mode (select-map-content icon).

label: Paint mode help text
summary: The tooltip text of the map content editor's paint (brush) button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the brush button, which is shown on pixel-based layers.

label: Remove-from-group help text
summary: The tooltip text of the map content editor's remove-from-group button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the remove-from-group button (brush-minus icon), which is shown on layers that are not pixel-based.

label: Is add-to-group mode
summary: Whether the map content editor is in add-to-group mode.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the add-to-group button (brush-plus icon), shown on layers that are not pixel-based.

label: Add-to-group allowed
summary: Whether the add-to-group mode of the map content editor can be used right now.
details: Vanilla enables the add-to-group button only while this is true. What it depends on is not stated.

label: Layer is pixel-based
summary: Whether the layer open in the map content editor is drawn pixel by pixel.
details: Vanilla shows the paint and eraser tools only for such layers (its comment calls them tools for pixel-based layers), and the add-to-group and remove-from-group tools only for the other layers (tools for group-based layers).

label: Is eraser mode
summary: Whether the map content editor is in eraser mode.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the eraser button; while the editor is in paint or eraser mode, the brush settings are shown.

label: Eraser mode allowed
summary: Whether the eraser mode of the map content editor may be used right now.
details: Vanilla enables the eraser button only when this and CanErase are both true; the game does not say how the two differ.

label: Is selection mode
summary: Whether the map content editor is in its selection mode.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the selection button (the select-map-content icon).

label: Selection mode allowed
summary: Whether the selection mode of the map content editor can be used right now.
details: Vanilla enables the selection button only while this is true.

label: Is paint mode
summary: Whether the map content editor is in paint (brush) mode.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the brush button; while the editor is in paint or eraser mode, the brush settings are shown.

label: Paint mode allowed
summary: Whether the paint mode of the map content editor may be used right now.
details: Vanilla enables the brush button only when this and IsPaintingAllowed are both true; the game does not say how the two differ.

label: Painting allowed
summary: Whether painting is possible right now in the map content editor.
details: Vanilla enables the brush button only when this and IsPaintModeAllowed are both true; the game does not say how the two differ.

label: Is remove-from-group mode
summary: Whether the map content editor is in remove-from-group mode.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the remove-from-group button (brush-minus icon), shown on layers that are not pixel-based.

label: Remove-from-group allowed
summary: Whether the remove-from-group mode of the map content editor can be used right now.
details: Vanilla enables the remove-from-group button only while this is true.

label: Editor options itself
summary: Gives the map content editor options itself, to pass them into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Use add-to-group mode
summary: Switches the map content editor into add-to-group mode.
details: Vanilla calls it from the add-to-group button (brush-plus icon), shown on layers that are not pixel-based.

label: Use eraser mode
summary: Switches the map content editor into eraser mode.
details: Vanilla calls it from the eraser button, shown on pixel-based layers.

label: Use selection mode
summary: Switches the map content editor's selection mode on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from the selection button with `'(bool)yes'`, which switches the mode on.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the selection mode is on.

label: Use paint mode
summary: Switches the map content editor into paint (brush) mode.
details: Vanilla calls it from the brush button, shown on pixel-based layers.

label: Use remove-from-group mode
summary: Switches the map content editor into remove-from-group mode.
details: Vanilla calls it from the remove-from-group button (brush-minus icon), shown on layers that are not pixel-based.

label: Viewport itself
summary: Gives the map content editor viewport itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Cancel property painting
summary: Stops property painting in the map content editor.
details: Property painting gives a chosen property value to what is clicked on the map. Vanilla calls this from the "Cancel (Esc)" button shown over the map while property painting is on.

label: Property painting text
summary: The text that describes the property painting going on in the map content editor.
details: Vanilla shows it in a box over the map while property painting is on, next to the "Cancel (Esc)" button.

label: Viewport tooltip
summary: The tooltip shown over the map in the map content editor.
details: It gives a GuiEditorTooltip object; vanilla's map editor tooltip shows its title and description when it has them.

label: Is property painting
summary: Whether property painting is on in the map content editor.
details: While it is on, vanilla shows a box over the map with the painting description and a "Cancel (Esc)" button. Property painting gives a chosen property value to what is clicked on the map.

label: Viewport itself
summary: Gives the map content editor viewport itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Entry itself
summary: Gives the map content entry description itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has errors
summary: Whether this map content entry has errors.
details: Vanilla shows an error mark on the entry's row in the map editor's entry list while this is true; its tooltip is the entry's error message.

label: Error message
summary: The error message of this map content entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the error mark on the entry's row.

label: Entry name
summary: The name of this map content entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of the entry's row in the map editor's list of entries (headed "All Territory entries").

label: Unique ID
summary: The unique number that identifies the map content entry.
details: It returns a whole number. Going by its name. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Is done
summary: Whether the map content entry is marked as done.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses IsDone on event chain progress entries to show a visible part; nothing uses it on this type.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this map content entry is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the entry's row; clicking the row tells the selector with OnEntrySelected.

label: This entry
summary: The map content entry itself, to hand it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to MapContentSelectorGui.OnEntrySelected when the entry's row is clicked.

label: Layer itself
summary: Gives the map content layer description itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Layer name
summary: The name of this map content layer.
details: Vanilla shows it as an option in the "Layer:" drop-down of the map editor, which chooses the layer to work on.

label: Layer itself
summary: Gives the map content layer description itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Panel itself
summary: Gives the map content panel itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can create entry
summary: Whether a new map content entry can be created right now.
details: Vanilla enables the map content panel's "Create" button only while this is true.

label: Can delete selected
summary: Whether at least one of the selected map content entries can be deleted.
details: Vanilla enables the map content panel's "Delete" button only while this is true.

label: Create entry
summary: Creates a new map content entry.
details: Vanilla calls it from the map content panel's "Create" button.

label: Delete selected entries
summary: Deletes the selected map content entries.
details: Vanilla calls it from the map content panel's "Delete" button.

label: Create button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the map content panel's "Create" button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the map content panel's "Create" button, which creates a new entry.

label: Delete button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the map content panel's "Delete" button.
details: Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the map content panel's "Delete" button, which deletes the selected entries.

label: Panel itself
summary: Gives the map content panel itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Property group itself
summary: Gives the map content property group itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Property group name
summary: The name of this group of properties in the map content editor.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading of the group, which can be folded open and shut.

label: Is expanded
summary: Whether this property group is folded open.
details: Vanilla uses it as the state of the group's fold button and shows the group's properties only while it is true.

label: Property group itself
summary: Gives the property group itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Fold or unfold group
summary: Folds this property group shut if it is open, or opens it if it is shut.
details: Vanilla calls it when the group's heading is clicked.

label: Property groups GUI itself
summary: Gives the property groups interface itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can start property painting
summary: Whether property painting can be started right now in the map content editor.
details: Vanilla enables the property painting buttons next to each property only while this is true. Property painting gives a property's value to what is clicked on the map.

label: Painting a yes/no property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given yes/no property.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to a yes/no property in the map content editor. Property painting gives this property's value to what is clicked on the map.

label: Painting a color property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given color property (the CColor kind).
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to a property of this color kind in the map content editor. A separate function covers the other color kind.

label: Painting a text property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given text property (the CString kind).
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to a property of this text kind in the map content editor. A separate function covers the other text kind (String).

label: Painting a color property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given color property.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to a color property in the map content editor. A separate function covers the CColor kind.

label: Painting a choice property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given choice property (one value picked from a fixed list).
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to such a property in the map content editor.

label: Painting a decimal property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given decimal-number property.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to a decimal-number property in the map content editor.

label: Painting a whole-number property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given whole-number property.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to a whole-number property in the map content editor.

label: Painting a text property
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given text property.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to a text property in the map content editor. A separate function covers the CString kind.

label: Painting a non-negative number
summary: Whether property painting is on for the given whole-number property that cannot be negative.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the property painting button next to such a property (uint) in the map content editor.

label: Property groups GUI itself
summary: Gives the property groups interface itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Toggle painting yes/no property
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given yes/no property.
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to a yes/no property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting color property
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given color property (the CColor kind).
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to such a property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting text property
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given text property (the CString kind).
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to such a property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting color property
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given color property.
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to a color property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting choice property
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given choice property (one value picked from a fixed list).
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to such a property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting decimal property
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given decimal-number property.
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to a decimal-number property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting whole number
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given whole-number property.
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to a whole-number property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting text property
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given text property.
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to a text property in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Toggle painting non-negative number
summary: Starts or stops property painting for the given whole-number property that cannot be negative.
details: Vanilla calls it from the property painting button next to such a property (uint) in the map content editor. While painting is on, clicking on the map gives that property's value to what is clicked.

label: Selector itself
summary: Gives the map content selector itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Error count
summary: The number of errors found in the map content selector.
details: It returns a whole number. Going by its name. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Selected count
summary: How many map content entries are selected.
details: Vanilla shows the property groups of the map content editor only while this is above 0.

label: All selected are done
summary: Whether every selected entry is marked as done.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: All selected have errors
summary: Whether every selected entry has errors.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Progress is shown
summary: Whether the selector currently shows progress.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Selector itself
summary: Gives the map content selector itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Mark selected as done
summary: Marks the selected entries as done or not done.
details: Going by its name; the one argument is probably a yes/no value, but the documentation does not say. It returns nothing. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; probably whether the selected entries are done, judging by the name.

label: Show progress
summary: Turns the display of progress in the selector on or off.
details: Going by its name; the one argument is probably a yes/no value, but the documentation does not say. It returns nothing. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; probably whether progress is shown, judging by the name.

label: Selector GUI itself
summary: Gives the map content selector interface itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Clear entries filter
summary: Empties the search filter of the map editor's entry list.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "X" button next to the filter box, with the tooltip "Clear filter."

label: Current layer
summary: Which layer is chosen in the map editor's "Layer:" drop-down.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected position of that drop-down. Its value is a pair of whole numbers (CVector2i); the game does not say what the two numbers stand for.

label: Entries filter
summary: The search text that filters the map editor's list of entries.
details: Vanilla shows it in the filter box; its tooltip says several search keys can be given, separated by `|`.

label: Entries with errors
summary: How many map content entries have errors.
details: Vanilla shows the number, in red, as the text of the button that filters the list down to entries with errors.

label: Selected entries
summary: How many map content entries are selected.
details: Vanilla enables some map editor tools only while it is above 0: a spline tool, and the auto-nudging of map objects (together with the nudger's own checks).

label: All selected done
summary: Whether every selected territory entry is marked as complete.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Mark all selected territory entries as complete"; clicking it flips the mark with SetSelectedDone.

label: All selected have errors
summary: Whether every selected entry has an error.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Error filter on
summary: Whether the map editor's entry list shows only entries with errors.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Filter all entries that contains errors."; clicking it flips the filter with SetFilterErrors.

label: Progress shown
summary: Whether the map highlights the territories marked as complete.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Highlight on the map territories marked as complete."; clicking it flips it with SetShowProgress.

label: Select entry
summary: Tells the map editor's entry list that the given entry was clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it when an entry's row is clicked, passing that entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a map content entry; vanilla passes `MapContentEntryDesc.Self`

label: Selector GUI itself
summary: Gives the map content selector interface itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set current layer
summary: Changes which layer the map editor works on.
details: Vanilla calls it when a different layer is picked in the "Layer:" drop-down; the drop-down hands over the new choice itself.

label: Set entries filter
summary: Sets the search text that filters the map editor's list of entries.
details: Vanilla calls it when typing in the filter box is finished; the box hands over its text. Several search keys can be separated by `|`.

label: Filter by errors
summary: Turns on or off the filter that shows only entries with errors.
details: Vanilla calls it from the error filter button, passing the opposite of IsFilterErrors, so a click toggles it.

label: Mark selected complete
summary: Marks the selected territory entries as complete, or takes the mark away.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Mark all selected territory entries as complete", passing the opposite of IsAllSelectedDone, so a click toggles the mark.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the entries are marked complete.

label: Show progress
summary: Turns on or off the map highlight of territories marked as complete.
details: Vanilla calls it from the progress button, passing the opposite of IsShowProgress, so a click toggles it.

label: Map editor itself
summary: Gives the map editor itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use AccessSelf, it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can toggle material visibility
summary: Whether the visibility of a material can be switched in the map editor.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Exit map editor
summary: Leaves the map editor, the game's built-in tool for editing the map.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Exit map editor".

label: Open export tool
summary: Opens the map editor's export tool.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Open the Export Tool" (its keyboard shortcut is named export_workspace).

label: Reference overlay shown
summary: Whether the map editor shows its reference overlay, a reference picture laid over the map.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the "Toggle reference texture overlay." button, and shows the overlay opacity setting only while it is true.

label: Terrain color map shown
summary: Whether the map editor shows the terrain color map overlay.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the button with the tooltip "Toggle terrain Color Map overlay."

label: Open import tool
summary: Opens the map editor's import tool.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button with the tooltip "Open the Import Tool" (its keyboard shortcut is named import_workspace).

label: Is auto-saving
summary: Whether the map editor is saving automatically right now.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla's top bar uses a plain IsAutoSaving (without the editor type) as the visibility of a part of the top bar; that is a different function, so it is only a hint.

label: Dynamic terrain switchable
summary: Whether the map editor's dynamic terrain materials feature can be switched on or off right now.
details: Vanilla enables the feature's switch only while this is true. The switch's tooltip says the feature needs fewer than 4 static materials.

label: Dynamic terrain on
summary: Whether the dynamic terrain materials feature is switched on in the map editor.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the feature's switch. While it is on, the material limit of 4 per detail pixel cannot be chosen. The switch's tooltip says the setting lasts only for the editor session and the game decides whether the feature is really on.

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether the map editor is enabled.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses IsEnabled on other types (music tracks and categories) as an on/off state, but not on this one.

label: Can be saved
summary: Whether the map editor can save right now.
details: Vanilla enables the map editor's "Save" button only while this is true. A disabled (commented-out) line in the GUI animation editor uses it the same way.

label: Reload heightmap
summary: Reloads the heightmap (the terrain height image) in the map editor.
details: Going by its name. It returns nothing. Nothing in vanilla uses it.

label: Reload material
summary: Loads the given material's texture again from its file on disk.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button in the map editor's materials list, with the tooltip "Reload this material texture from disk".

label: Save
summary: Saves the work in the map editor.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Save" button, which works only while IsSavable is true.

label: Save all
summary: Saves everything open in the map editor.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Save all" button.

label: Save as
summary: Saves the work in the map editor under a name or place to choose.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Save as" button.

label: Map editor itself
summary: Gives the map editor itself, to pass it into another function.
details: Going by its name and the way other types use Self (for example Character.Self given as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Switch dynamic terrain
summary: Switches the map editor's dynamic terrain materials feature on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from the feature's switch, passing the opposite of IsDynamicTerrainMaterialSupported. The tooltip says it needs fewer than 4 static materials, lasts only for the editor session, and the game still decides whether the feature is really on.
